comments.text: Thank you so much for covering Logan's story. I am from Tumwater WA. My kids attend THS, and this story is so heartbreaking for the community . We drive by his and others missing posters every day:(He is not the only young man to have gone missing from the Thurston county area in the last 10 years. Other male teens have as well.  Matthew Anfeldt went missing is 2019 and his partial remains were just found by a hunter in Rochester-Grandmound in 2023. He had been missing since 2019. His story is also bizarre. I also wanted to point out that I used to live right across from the "Olympia airport", and it's right along a long stretch of road where I have pulled over many times to look for something in my car, take a phone call..ect.. So  it could've said he was "at the airport" when he just pulled in to stop for a minute,  there are also 2 different gas station's right next to the airport. So it may have looked like he was at the airport, but was stopped at the store,🤷and this airport isn't some giant airport, its a small airport for  private plans, helicopter's, and there is a flight school there as well. So it isn't an international airport where you buy a ticket and fly to wherever. You would either be attending flight school there, or you would need to know someone with a small private plane to take you somewhere.. It is not a commercial airline service. I'm just trying to put it into perspective for those who think he arrived at an airport booked a flight and took off, because you can't do that there. 🙏

comments.text:
I really enjoy this series of videos. I also want to say, for anyone who read it, I'm 52 now, but was adopted & although I wasn't very curious about my immediate biological family, I did have a real interest in my ancestral heritage. And over all the years of my life, talking to other about that, the people who often had the same interest, in the way that I did, were often people of color, of mixed heritage, whether they were the children of a black parent & a white parent, or Asian, or First Nations, etc. I think families who have even one mixed race kid in their families, do them a disservice when they try to just "love them enough" to make them less aware of being "different." And the opposite, trying to convince them that "we're all mixed race," while accurate, doesn't help. 

If you have a young person in your family who isn't sure about where they fit, you can help them navigate that by learning together. Your father is from the Middle East, but doesn't care about you? Screw him then, but maybe let's look at some books abou that part of the world, see if anything seems cool to you, & then we'll study it. In a way, my love of all things Irish is what led me to Mike's channel, cuz my daughter found him first & knew I'd want to see his content.

comments.text: The story of the Jack family is so heart-breaking.  I can very easily see how the conversation went:  some small talk, then talk of 'what do you do', 'looking for a job', and a serial killers alarm goes off.  He thinks he can now get 2 for 1.  Both are desperate to work so would be easy to string them along.  And then finds out about the kids - he probably asked if there was someone who could take care of them.  When the brother said no, he thought "don't want the guy talking to too many people here trying to find a sitter - best to just get them the hell out of here as fast as I can" and so then he adds the "we have daycare" comment.  There.  Nice, neat, tidy situation.....for a murderer.  In a real world situation, the stranger would say "hey my company is looking for people - here is a phone number you can call".  No one can accept employees on behalf of another person's company.  Secondly,  to tell that potential employee that you will take him tonight to the logging camp is so sketchy.  I feel so bad for the family that they were so desperate that they overlooked all of danger signs.  😞

The Pickering boys: a lake crossing a border  = smuggling traffic. I'm assuming that they stumbled across a late-night smuggler loading or unloading and were disposed of. The police were probably either paid off or involved in the business themselves (not uncommon at the border), and stonewalled to keep themselves in the clear.
Yeah, it's the relatively clean Canada/U.S. border, but drugs and cigarettes at a minimum are big smuggling items.
As many people have said, them stealing a boat and dying of young stupidity or just misfortune in the lake is absolutely a possibility, but for not a single body or bit of clothing or bit of a legendarily unsinkable boat to ever be found makes it less likely. Even if they went overboard and sank without a trace, that boat would be out there. Pieces of it at the very least.

comments.text: I really don’t think that you get the scale of The Great Lakes in the USA. We refer to them as inland seas, and do so for a reason. They swallow tankers and ore ships and leave no trace of them. Even wooden ships go down with no debris field. A little boat with six people on it could get swamped and leave nothing behind, then scatter the bodies so far and wide that they could never be found. We aren’t talking about a pleasure lake here, a place you go to fish and/or ski, or put around. There are more boats and bodies at the bottom of The Great Lakes than there are in most shipwreck areas on the ocean…..
